2) What is the recommended flow for certificate issuance and rotation for the client-facing hostname (we prefer client-side validation/MTLS)?

Hi Sam — thanks for the CSRs. Short answer up front: Acme should own the private DNS zone and the FQDN records (zone delegation), Redwood will provide the CSR templates, validate the PKI chain, and accept the certificate for server identity. For mTLS, both sides must exchange/trust the same CA roots (or configure a trust bundle).

I attached a concise checklist (redwood-private-dns-checklist.pdf) that maps each step to owner and risk notes. High-level:
- Acme: provision private zone (redwood.acme.internal), create A/AAAA or CNAME to your edge load balancer, and publish the OCSP responder entry if you have one.
- Acme: provide CSR signed by your CA or have Redwood generate CSR and Acme signs it (we prefer customer-signed CSRs for customer-controlled keys).
- Redwood: verify CSR, sign with our intermediate (if configured), or accept customer-signed cert and install to private endpoint.
- Joint: agree rotation cadence and emergency rollback procedure (we recommend automated rotation every 90 days for short-lived certs).

Next step: quick 30-min call to walk the infra engineer through the checklist and confirm DNS ACLs/zone transfers. Are you available Fri 11/27 10am PT?

Attachments: redwood-private-dns-checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Sam — adding a few infra-level clarifications we ran into with other customers that might affect your zone delegation approach: 

- Split-horizon: If Acme uses split-horizon DNS, ensure the internal view exposes the private FQDN to Redwood peering subnets / VPN CIDR. Otherwise our health checks and K/V cache warming will fail.
- FQDN ownership: In practice, customers keep the apex (acme.internal) but create a subzone (redwood.acme.internal) and delegate NXDOMAIN responses to the edge. Delegation via NS records works well.
- Certificate trust: For mutual TLS, either: (a) Acme provides a CA bundle we trust on our side (recommended), or (b) we configure an intermediary that accepts customer-signed leaf certs — this increases operational complexity.

I'll join the call if we need to walk through zone files. Jonas — can you draft a minimal automation snippet (ansible/bash) to generate the CSR template, create the cert resource in our private endpoint, and validate TLS end-to-end?

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha King <sking@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment - who claims root/private-hostname?

Marissa / Stephanie / Sam — draft runbook & quick automation below. I attached a delegation matrix (doc-dns-delegation-matrix.xlsx) to map steps. Pasteable steps: 

1) Acme: create subzone redwood.acme.internal and add NS entries pointing to your authoritative servers for that subzone.
2) Acme: create A record for edge (edge-01.redwood.acme.internal -> 10.4.2.8) and ensure the firewall allows Redwood peering IPs.
3) Acme: either: (A) generate CSR locally using provided template and sign with Acme CA, upload signed cert to Redwood Console -> Private Endpoints -> Certificates, or (B) issue API call to Redwood to generate CSR and return CSR PEM for you to sign.
4) Redwood: run tls-check utility (included in runbook) to validate: chain, CN/SAN, OCSP stapling (if present), and cipher policy.
5) Joint: schedule rotation job (cron) that calls Redwood API to fetch cert install status and roll back if validation fails.

Small automation snippet (bash/openssl):
-----BEGIN SNIPPET-----
# gen csr and private key
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -out redwood_acme.csr -keyout redwood_acme.key -subj "/CN=edge-01.redwood.acme.internal/O=Acme Corp"
# sample API call to upload and mark active (pseudo)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -F "cert=@redwood_acme.crt" -F "key=@redwood_acme.key" https://console.redwood.example/api/private/endpoints/edge-01/certs
-----END SNIPPET-----

Sam — if you want, we can push a small repo with the snippet plus the tls-checker. We can also add a preflight step to validate split-horizon visibility from Redwood egress points.

—Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
